ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: If the center of gravity of the blades of an electric fan is not on the rotating shaft, when rotating it will make the fan shake and accelerate wear of the rotating shaft. When adjusting, small metal blocks can be fixed in a certain region of the blades to change the position of its center of gravity. A and B are two metal blocks for adjusting the center of gravity (which can be regarded as point masses), their masses are equal, and their distances to the rotating shaft O satisfy rA＜rB. After the blades rotate, what is the size relationship between the centripetal forces FA and FB experienced by the two metal blocks A and B?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the blades and central hub of an electric fan, and marks the rotating shaft O; the two small black dots A and B represent metal blocks fixed on the blades/hub, at different positions. Combining with the conditions given in the question stem, A and B can be regarded as point masses, their masses are equal, and their distances to the rotating shaft O satisfy rA＜rB. Reasoning: After the blades rotate, both A and B move in circular motion around O together with the same fan, so the angular velocity ω is the same. The centripetal force formula is F=mω²r. Because m is the same and ω is the same, the magnitude of the centripetal force is only directly proportional to the radius r; moreover rA＜rB, so FA＜FB.

method.method_draft: 先从图像读出风扇绕中心转轴 O 转动，金属块 A、B 固定在扇叶/轮毂上的不同位置；再结合题干给出的关键条件：A、B 可视为质点，质量相等，且到转轴的距离满足 rA＜rB。风扇转动时两金属块与扇叶一起做同角速度圆周运动，因此使用向心力公式 F=mω²r。由于 m 相同、ω 相同，向心力只随半径 r 增大而增大，所以 rA＜rB 推出 FA＜FB。
